summary: A single full-screen canvas (PIXI/WebGL) that plays a sequence of animated scenes made with Leon Sans, a geometric sans drawn entirely in code as a JavaScript library: the name is drawn stroke by stroke, gains weight, the camera zooms into the letters, then glyphs are drawn, dropped with physics into a liquid floor and finally written in multicoloured strokes. There is no text on the page except the canvas and a GitHub corner icon.

instances.look: On white, 'LEON SANS' in hairline caps (~60px) is drawn on stroke by stroke from the centre, thickens to a bold weight, then the view zooms until thin 'N SA' and finally 'SA' fill and overflow the screen
instances.ux: Plays by itself after load (the capture's wheel events may also step it); nothing to click except the GitHub corner icon
instances.learn: For a font that is code, show the drawing itself: stroke draw-on, live weight change and a camera zoom prove the glyphs are parametric, not static outlines

reconstruction.layout: One canvas 100vw × 100vh (devicePixelRatio 2); name centred horizontally at ~48% height, letter-spaced caps ~360px wide; zoom stage scales the word until two letters are ~560px tall (01) then ~830px (02), cropped by the viewport
reconstruction.typography: Leon Sans rendered as canvas strokes: caps, start weight ~1 (hairline), animated to ~7–8 (bold) with tracking ~0.2em; at zoom the stroke stays hairline-to-light (~6px at 560px cap height)
reconstruction.behaviour: Timeline: blank white ~1.5s; strokes draw on letter by letter (~2s, each path's drawing progress 0 → 1); weight tweens to bold (~1.5s); camera scale tween zooms into 'SA' (~2s); hard cut to black for the next scene. Leon Sans API: new LeonSans({text, size, weight, tracking}) with drawing animation via each path's 'drawing' value (GSAP tween)
reconstruction.assets: Leon Sans JS library (github.com/cmiscm/leonsans); PIXI.js canvas
reconstruction.html: div#root > canvas#canvas (2880×1800 backing for 1440×900); a#git GitHub SVG icon fixed top-right; new LeonSansApp() on window.onload

instances.look: Black scenes: a white rounded 'B' (~260px) is drawn on from a single arc, sinks into a wavy white liquid floor rising from the bottom while capitals (K, W, J, O, Z, H, Y, &) rain from the top with physics; then white, and (video only, t≈19–21s) the word 'composition' written in multicoloured dashed strokes
instances.ux: Watch-only sequence; each scene demonstrates a different capability of the code font (draw-on, rounded weight, physics bodies, fluid/metaball floor, colour pattern strokes)
instances.learn: When the font is a library, the specimen is a reel of demos: each scene shows one thing you can do with the glyph paths (animate, collide, melt, recolour)

reconstruction.layout: Same full-screen canvas; single glyph centred (~260px cap height, 520px in 2x) then sinking to the bottom; falling letters ~100–140px scattered across the top half; white fluid band ~20–200px tall along the bottom edge with a wobbling top
reconstruction.typography: Leon Sans caps with round caps and joins, white strokes ~14px at 260px size on black; final word lowercase ~70px in rainbow-coloured stroke segments on white
reconstruction.behaviour: Scene 1: 'B' drawn on (path progress) then weight-in; scene 2: glyphs become rigid bodies (Matter.js-style physics) falling and tumbling onto a liquid metaball floor that rises and swallows them; scene 3: cross-fade to white, 'composition' drawn with a colour pattern along each stroke. Auto-advancing, ~4–5s per scene, loops
reconstruction.content: Single letters and one word ('composition'); no copy
reconstruction.assets: Leon Sans library, a 2D physics engine and a metaball/fluid shader (PIXI filters)
reconstruction.html: Everything is drawn into canvas#canvas; no DOM text

instances.look: Not cut as a block: a ~16px GitHub octocat icon fixed in the top-right corner (black on white scenes, white on black) linking to the Leon Sans repository, the site's only link
